subsystems.name: Optical frequency reference
subsystems.role: the clock itself — a narrow optical transition in a trapped ion or thousands of neutral atoms held in an optical lattice.
parts: interrogation laser locked to a stable cavity

subsystems.name: Optical frequency comb
subsystems.role: converts the ~10^15 Hz optical signal down to countable microwave or telecom rates so it can be counted and transported.

subsystems.name: Fibre transport link
subsystems.role: carries the signal phase-coherently hundreds or thousands of kilometres without the noise of free-space or satellite links.

subsystems.name: Comparison electronics
subsystems.role: measures the ratio between two clocks with fractional uncertainty near 10^-18.

subsystems.name: Modelling and geodesy layer
subsystems.role: turns frequency ratios into gravitational potential differences and geoid data.

buildSteps.title: Build the clocks
buildSteps.detail: Laser-cool atoms to microkelvin temperatures in an ultra-high vacuum, then trap them — in an optical lattice for neutral atoms or an electromagnetic trap for a single ion.

buildSteps.title: Narrow the probe laser
buildSteps.detail: Lock a laser to a vibration-isolated optical cavity so its linewidth is well below the atomic transition, giving interrogation times of seconds.

buildSteps.title: Stabilise the comb
buildSteps.detail: A femtosecond laser's pulse train is broadened to an octave and self-referenced, tying the optical frequency to the microwave domain and to the existing caesium standard.

buildSteps.title: Link the sites
buildSteps.detail: Dedicated dark fibre is laid or leased between laboratories; bidirectional amplifiers and active phase-noise cancellation undo the fibre's thermal and acoustic jitter.

buildSteps.title: Validate the link
buildSteps.detail: Two clocks at the same site are compared over the link path first, to prove the transport adds no measurable error.

buildSteps.title: Run continuously
buildSteps.detail: Clocks are compared for days or weeks; statistical uncertainty falls with averaging time, reaching 10^-18 and below.

buildSteps.title: Interpret the ratio
buildSteps.detail: A frequency difference is read as a gravitational redshift, which converts directly into a height difference — the inverse of levelling.

buildSteps.title: Cross-check and publish
buildSteps.detail: Results are validated against GNSS, spirit levelling and gravimetry before entering the data pool for the SI second.

prerequisites.why: atoms must be nearly motionless for their transition frequency to be sharp.
without them an optical frequency cannot be counted or transported alongside microwave standards.
the probe laser's stability sets the short-term precision of the comparison.
long links must be actively corrected, or the fibre itself swamps the clock signal.

prerequisites.tech: Secondary representations of the second and an agreed redefinition path
prerequisites.why: optical clocks cannot define the second until several independent types agree and uncertainty budgets are settled.

pathway.milestone: continental fibre links between metrology laboratories — including a roughly 1400 km route between German and French institutes — routinely compare optical clocks
pathway.unlocks: frequency transfer good enough for centimetre-level height measurement and tests of fundamental constants.

pathway.milestone: national dark-fibre networks open to many institutions, as in the French research network
pathway.unlocks: routine relativistic geodesy, monitoring of uplift, subsidence and groundwater loss.

pathway.milestone: transportable optical clocks taken to the sites being measured
pathway.unlocks: geodesy far from any dedicated fibre, and direct validation against classical levelling.

pathway.milestone: redefinition of the SI second on an optical transition
pathway.unlocks: a global time and frequency infrastructure accurate enough to search for dark-matter couplings and drift in fundamental constants.

pathway.milestone: operational clock networks combining fibre and space links
pathway.unlocks: real-time height and gravity services, better sea-level and earthquake reference frames.
